runs.name: contract question answering
runs.goal: Contract question answering for a 200-person professional services firm: locate and quote clauses in executed contracts with citations, or refuse and name a person.
runs.fixtureNote: Worked example shipped with the AI Architect plugin. Paths, commands and observed outputs are this example's definition, not a recording from a live repository. Re-derive everything against your own repository before treating any line as evidence.
runs.outcome: Anyone in the firm can ask a question about an executed contract and get an answer that cites the exact clauses it rests on, or a refusal that names who to ask instead.
runs.killCriterion: If, after six weeks of use, the share of answers that the legal ops lead's weekly sample of 40 finds correct and correctly cited is below 34 of 40, measured on 2026-10-11 with node scripts/citation-audit.mjs --sample 40 --since 2026-08-30, the system is turned off. Not retuned: turned off. A contract answer that is usually right is a liability, because it teaches people to stop checking.

runs.name: support triage
runs.goal: Triage the inbound support inbox of a 40-person B2B software company: classify, route, and draft a reply that a support agent approves before anything sends.
runs.fixtureNote: Worked example shipped with the AI Architect plugin. Paths, commands and observed outputs are this example's definition, not a recording from a live repository. Re-derive everything against your own repository before treating any line as evidence.
runs.outcome: Every inbound support email is classified, routed to a queue, and answered with a drafted reply that a support agent approves before anything leaves the building.
runs.killCriterion: If, after four full weeks in production, the share of drafted replies that support agents send without editing the body is below one in three, measured on 2026-10-04 from the support platform's revision history, the drafting step is removed and only classification and routing stay. Measurement command and its owner are in 07-runbook.md, step 6.

packages/prompt/src/build.ts:L27 — ticket body wrapped as <untrusted_ticket> in the user message; system message built at packages/prompt/src/system.ts:L14. ADR-0001.
apps/worker/src/queue.ts:L11 — queued worker; longest observed run 41 s against a 300 s request-scoped ceiling. ADR-0002.

runs.name: personal AI centre of excellence
runs.goal: Build a personal AI centre of excellence on one person's own machine: three scheduled loops, a local memory store, and an ad-hoc session mode, with every output read by the operator before it becomes a decision.
runs.fixtureNote: Worked example shipped with the AI Architect plugin. Paths, commands and observed outputs are this example's definition, not a recording from a live machine. Re-derive everything against your own machine before treating any line as evidence.
runs.outcome: One person's routine reading, sorting and recall runs as three scheduled loops on their own machine, and every output is a draft that person reads before it becomes a decision.
runs.killCriterion: If the morning brief is opened on fewer than 20 of the next 30 days, measured on 2026-09-22 from the run log at ~/.coe/runs/brief.jsonl with node scripts/brief-open-rate.mjs --last 30, the scheduled loops are deleted and only ad-hoc sessions stay. An unread brief is not a tuning problem; it is a system nobody wanted.

finding.title: F1 — the restore path has never run, and gate.operate is red because of it.
fix: Install the snapshot backup tool the backup script already writes for, restore to a scratch target, and record the exit status in the runbook table. Fixture estimate: 40 minutes.

Or remove the dependency: schedule node scripts/memory-export.mjs nightly, dry-run scripts/memory-import.mjs, and record the exit status. Fixture estimate: 90 minutes, and the system ends up with one fewer external tool.
